name: Translator
seoDescription: Calculate estimated business insurance costs for translator businesses including general liability and professional E&O coverage.

industryContext.contextNote: Translators convert content between languages with no physical work product, so their exposure is narrowly focused on translation accuracy in high-stakes documents.

riskFactors.title: Mistranslation in Legal or Medical Documents
riskFactors.description: An inaccurate translation of a legal contract or medical record can cause serious downstream harm to the parties relying on it.

riskFactors.title: Missed Deadline Disputes
riskFactors.description: Time-sensitive translations for legal filings or business deals can trigger disputes if delivered late.

riskFactors.title: Confidential Document Handling
riskFactors.description: Translators often handle sensitive legal, medical, or business documents, creating liability if that content is mishandled or disclosed.

faqs.question: Why do translators need Errors & Omissions insurance?
faqs.answer: E&O covers claims that a translation error caused financial or legal harm, which is especially important for legal, medical, or technical translation work.

faqs.question: What is the average cost of business insurance for a translator?
faqs.answer: A translator in the $0-50k revenue tier pays an estimated $245 per year for baseline General Liability coverage, among the lowest tiers modeled here.

faqs.question: Do certified court translators need different coverage?
faqs.answer: Court and legal translators often face stricter client requirements for E&O coverage given the high stakes of legal document accuracy.

faqs.question: Is General Liability necessary for a translator who works entirely remotely?
faqs.answer: Many clients require proof of General Liability in contracts regardless of remote work status, even though physical premises risk is minimal for this profession.

blogContent.whyThisRiskFactor: Translators carry a 0.8 actuarial risk factor, among the lowest in the calculator, reflecting minimal physical hazard and narrowly scoped professional-liability exposure.
blogContent.howCalculated: Premiums scale with revenue tier, with Professional Liability (E&O) as the primary and often only relevant endorsement.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Translator premiums are among the lowest of any profession here, matching copywriters and graphic designers.
